notes.3: Many candidates appreciated that the root hair cell has a cell wall and a sperm cell does not. Some candidates incorrectly believed that root hair cells contain chloroplasts.
notes.5: Only a minority of candidates appreciated that the movement of glucose molecules into the epithelium and the movement of nitrate ions from a dilute solution in soil into a more concentrated solution in root hairs require oxygen. notes.11: Most candidates incorrectly believed that the hydrogencarbonate indicator in test-tube A would turn yellow. Since the leaves in test-tube A were exposed to light, photosynthesis would occur, removing carbon dioxide from inside the test-tube. An increase in carbon dioxide is required to turn the hydrogencarbonate indicator yellow, which occurs in test-tube B . In this test-tube, the leaves are in the dark and respiring, giving off carbon dioxide.
notes.13: This was a demanding question with only a minority of candidates selecting correctly. Candidates need to appreciate that a reduction of chloride ions in a solution will increase the water potential.
notes.14: Few candidates appreciated that at X, maltose is broken down by maltase and therefore the concentration of maltose is decreasing.
notes.16: Some candidates correctly interpreted the diagram and understood that the phloem vessels have been removed and sucrose cannot move to the sink.
notes.17: Most candidates were able to identify the coronary artery.
notes.20: The approximate percentage of oxygen (16%) in expired air was not widely known.
notes.22: While most candidates knew the word equation for anaerobic respiration in yeast, some candidates incorrectly believed that lactic acid is produced.
notes.23: Many candidates were aware that carbon dioxide, urea and water are excreted from the human body. Some candidates incorrectly selected option A , carbon dioxide and urea only.
notes.24: Many candidates appreciated that glucagon will cause the body to convert glycogen into glucose. Some candidates incorrectly believed that insulin would cause the body to convert glycogen into glucose.
notes.27: Most candidates did not appreciate that non-bacterial and viral diseases cannot be treated with antibiotics.
notes.28: Many candidates appreciated that plantlets are produced by mitosis and are genetically identical. Some candidates incorrectly believed that plantlets are produced by meiosis.
notes.29: Most candidates knew that the male gamete has an acrosome and is motile.
